records.summary: The idea is an API and searchable feed that maps Employment Rights Act commencement instruments to effective dates. Payroll and HR software vendors would use it to track implementation changes.

competitors.name: GOV.UK Employment Rights Act implementation timeline
competitors.note: The kill-check says it already maps measures to commencement dates, including the January 2027 changes.

competitors.name: The Legal Brief tracker
competitors.note: Free tracker; last updated August 2026.

competitors.name: WPC HR tracker
competitors.note: Detailed tracker published 14 October 2026.

competitors.name: PaySoft
competitors.note: The sources describe ERA-related payroll features as new in April 2026.

competitors.name: Employment Hero HR and Employment Law Advisory
competitors.note: Adjacent employment-compliance product, not a vendor-focused feed.

competitors.name: HRConnect implementation and training service
competitors.note: Adjacent service listed in its Spring 2026 catalogue.

competitors.name: Statuta
competitors.note: Quotes white-label compliance by client-book size; no fixed price found.

rounds.plain: GOV.UK provides a free implementation timeline that covers the core need of mapping measures to commencement dates.

risks: Vendor demand and willingness to pay are unverified.
Official dates can change; stale or incorrectly labelled legal status could damage trust.
A status-aware interpretation layer and reliable integrations might create switching costs, but neither exists yet.
Owner workload and automation level are unverified.
records.moat: Raw legislation and dates are not proprietary. A carefully versioned mapping with evidence, transitional rules, status distinctions, and vendor integrations could create some switching cost after adoption, but this asset does not yet exist.
records.next_steps: Make a static three-event JSON sample with source and status fields, present it with a vendor-facing explanation and opt-in pilot request, and count success only if a payroll or HR software vendor requests integration details and agrees in writing to a paid pilot.

records.summary: The idea is a machine-readable change feed and impact checklist for new Ofcom duties under the Online Safety Act. Small online service operators would pay to track policy changes and assess their impact.

competitors.name: Ofcom Online Safety industry bulletin
competitors.note: The kill-check says it provides industry updates.

competitors.name: Ofcom digital safety toolkit and compliance checker
competitors.note: The kill-check says these tools provide step-by-step compliance help.

rounds.plain: Ofcom already publishes a free industry bulletin and compliance tools that cover the core update and impact-checklist need.

risks: Demand for a separate feed and willingness to pay are unverified.
The new takedown duty is a planned consultation with a 2027 target, not a verified commencement date.
The cited additional risk-assessment duties target Category 1 and 2A services, so relevance to small platforms is unverified.

records.paid_demand: The sources confirm that Enhanced Media Library has a paid PRO version, but its price is unverified. The listing also reports 60,000+ active installs; that is not evidence of paid customers.

records.summary: The business is a visual workflow SaaS for SEO agencies and content teams. It offers AI content workflows through subscriptions and usage credits.
records.how_money: Subscriptions and usage credits; listing says plans are $20/$75/$200, but does not specify currency.

revenue_claims.claim: $600 last-month revenue and $500 profit; the listing's connected-metrics section says fewer than 10 customers and $0 ARR, while its narrative says 5 paying customers. Payment records are not publicly visible.
$21.6k TTM revenue and $14k TTM profit; listing narrative also says the business is loss-making on the TTM P&L.
About $3k MRR at an earlier point, followed by a decline after marketing stopped.

records.paid_demand: The seller reports 5 paying customers and $600 last-month revenue, but the payment records are not publicly visible. The listing's connected metrics also say $0 ARR, and its TTM profit and loss claims conflict.

competitors.name: AirOps
competitors.note: Named direct competitor; the sources also say thousands of marketers have used its product.

competitors.name: ArgSEO
competitors.note: SEO automation product introduced May 30, 2026.

competitors.name: GPTMelo
competitors.note: SEO/GEO workflow platform announced June 23, 2026.

competitors.name: Quattr
competitors.note: Adjacent supervised AI landing-page workflow launched May 8, 2026.

rounds.plain: The kill-check found no kill rule and cited the seller's reported five payers, $600 last-month revenue, and under five hours per month of current operations; these claims are unverified.
Multiple competing SEO workflow products launched within the six-month window, including ArgSEO and GPTMelo. Recent revenue is unverified, and the older claimed MRR decline gets zero weight.

risks: Financial figures conflict within the listing and are not independently verified.
Only 5 payers are reported against 6,000 reported signups.
The AngularJS stack is end-of-life, creating possible maintenance or migration work.
Automation share and the ability to run the business within 5 h/week are unverified.
Bulk AI content faces Google scaled-content-abuse rules when used primarily to manipulate rankings without user value.
records.moat: Potential assets include the workflow engine, reported 30+ templates, integrations, customer personas and knowledge bases, domain, and signup list. With only 5 reported payers, meaningful switching costs are unproven.

hours.note: Seller claim for running it as-is; unverified and excludes unknown growth and support workload.

records.next_steps: Request the data room and reconcile dated Stripe transactions, customer metrics, monthly P&L, and cloud bills. Confirm the 5 payers, $600 monthly revenue, $0 ARR, and TTM profit/loss discrepancy; inspect analytics and technical deployment before considering a purchase.

records.summary: The business is a marketing analytics SaaS that helps businesses compare Google Ads and organic search performance. The listing is for a product described as a read-only Google data dashboard.

records.customer: Businesses using Google Ads and organic search
records.market: UK market evidence includes entities using Google search advertising; the product's precise geographic market is not stated.
records.paid_demand: The Acquire listing states $5,000 annual revenue and $1,000 annual profit, but provides no dated revenue period or transaction proof. No independent payment evidence is given.

competitors.name: Google Ads Paid and Organic report
competitors.note: Google provides a native paid-and-organic report after linking Search Console.

competitors.name: Google Analytics
competitors.note: Provides paid/organic channel reporting; exact plan eligibility is unverified.

competitors.name: Keyword Ninja
competitors.note: Its help page documents an Ads/Search Console comparison.

competitors.name: Looker Studio dashboard template
competitors.note: Price unverified.

competitors.note: Adjacent reporting alternative.

competitors.name: AgencyAnalytics
competitors.note: Adjacent reporting alternative.

competitors.name: Whatagraph
competitors.note: Adjacent reporting alternative.

rounds.plain: Google already provides paid-and-organic reporting in Google Ads and paid/organic channel reporting in Analytics, covering the stated comparison need.

risks: The seller's revenue and profit claims are unverified; the stated $1,000 annual profit against a $13,000 asking price is 13x profit.
Owner hours and automation share are unverified.
The product depends on Google Ads and Search Console access, APIs, quotas, and OAuth requirements.
The free Google report and Keyword Ninja comparison may substitute for the product's core function.
records.moat: No defensible asset is evidenced in the public listing. It describes a read-only Google data dashboard without documented proprietary data, rules engine, benchmarks, switching costs, or customer retention.

budget.note: Asking price in the listing summary.

records.next_steps: Ask the seller for a read-only demo using a representative account and compare its output with Google's Paid and Organic report and Keyword Ninja's free comparison. Request dated payment evidence and an operator task/time log; proceed only if the demo shows a valuable, reproducible insight unavailable in the free substitutes.
